NCLEX Practice Questions
4 questions generated from source material.
Questions
1. A client with heart failure has a serum potassium of 3.1 mEq/L and is scheduled to receive digoxin 0.125 mg and
furosemide 40 mg this morning. Which action should the nurse take first? A. Give the scheduled furosemide B.
Hold digoxin and notify the provider C. Encourage oral fluids D. Recheck the potassium in the morning
2. Which findings indicate fluid volume overload? Select all that apply. A. Crackles in the lung bases B. Weight gain
of 2 kg in 2 days C. Poor skin turgor D. Jugular venous distension E. Concentrated urine
3. Place the steps for auscultating heart sounds in the correct order. ___ Mitral area ___ Aortic area ___ Erb's point
___ Pulmonic area
4. The provider orders 1,000 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride to infuse over 8 hours. The client's labs: 1. Sodium 138
mEq/L 2. Potassium 4.0 mEq/L At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Answer: __________ mL/hr
10/9/26, 1:40 PM NCLEX-Practice-Questions-4-questions
http://127.0.0.1:8765/file?name=ws.html 1/2
Answer Key
1. ANSWER: B Why A is wrong: Furosemide lowers potassium further and raises toxicity risk. (Source: C2) Why B is
correct: Hypokalemia raises digoxin toxicity risk, so the dose is held and the provider notified. (Source: C1 — "low
potassium increases digoxin toxicity") Why C is wrong: Fluids do not correct potassium. (Source: C3) Why D is
wrong: Delays care. (Source: C3) Strategy: Safety first. Tags: Tier 1 | Recognize Cues | Cardiac::HF
2. ANSWER: A, B, D Why A is correct: Crackles mean fluid in the alveoli. (Source: C4) Why B is correct: Rapid gain is
fluid. (Source: C4) Why C is wrong: Poor turgor is deficit. (Source: C5) Why D is correct: JVD means overload.
(Source: C4) Why E is wrong: Concentrated urine is deficit. (Source: C5) Tags: Tier 2 | Analyze Cues
3. ANSWER: Aortic area → Pulmonic area → Erb's point → Mitral area 1. Aortic area — base of the heart first.
(Source: C6) 2. Pulmonic area — second left intercostal space. (Source: C6) 3. Erb's point — third left intercostal
space. (Source: C6) 4. Mitral area — apex last. (Source: C6) Tags: Tier 3
4. ANSWER: 125 mL/hr 1,000 mL ÷ 8 hr = 125 mL/hr (Source: C7) Strategy: Volume over time. Tags: Tier 1 | Take
Action

NCLEX Practice Questions
4 questions generated from source material.
Questions
1. A client receiving an intravenous infusion reports burning at the site. Which action should the nurse take first?
A. Stop the infusion and assess the site. B. Slow the rate and recheck the site by 2. C. Apply a warm compress and
continue the infusion. D. Document the finding and notify the next shift.
2. Which findings indicate dehydration in an older adult? Select all that apply.
3. Dry mucous membranes
4. Bounding peripheral pulses
5. Increased serum sodium
6. New onset confusion
7. Jugular venous distension
8. Place the steps for inserting a urinary catheter in the correct order. ___ Perform hand hygiene ___ Clean the
meatus ___ Insert the catheter ___ Inflate the balloon
9. A client with hypoglycemia is awake and able to swallow. Which action should the nurse take?
A. Give 15 g of a fast-acting carbohydrate. B. Administer glucagon intramuscularly. C. Withhold food until the
next meal. D. Start an insulin infusion.

Answer Key
1. ANSWER: A Why A is correct: Burning at the site suggests infiltration, so stopping the infusion and assessing the
site comes first. (Source: C1) Why B is wrong: Slowing the rate does not address possible infiltration at the site.
(Source: C2) Why C is wrong: A warm compress with a continued infusion worsens infiltration. (Source: C2) Why
